I avoided using diamonds in the example since they aren't actually rare or worth anything for scarcity, but for marketing and supply control.

I guarantee it doesn't play the part. A watch like this is certified which means that it is loses no more than -4/+6 seconds a day. It's pretty common for these fakes to gain/lose minutes a day. I have a certified watch and it only loses a second a week. The fake would be 5 minutes off in a week.

Also, I would wager that in 10 years you might be throwing the replica in the trash because it a) is breaking down because it's a weird original franken movement built to trick the eye not for actual durability / performance and b) no one can work on it because they aren't familiar with the movement / don't want to work on fakes.

To be fair, outside of luxury timepieces, I never get comments on my watches at all. My friends wearing their affordable brands, or fashion quartz watches get way more complements from random people than my premium brands, or even my luxury watch really.
